text:
Ava (Eng Manager): Hey folks — new PM-starting infra engineer joins in two weeks. Can someone post a short, copy/paste manager checklist that covers prestart, a granular first-14-days plan (not just week1), a crisp 30/60/90 with measurable outcomes, and the exact people to ping for access/equipment? Want something I can drop into a calendar invite and share with skip-level.
Rhea (People Ops): Hi @Ava — posted a compact "Manager Mini-Sprint" below you can reuse. I also created calendar templates and will DM the Slack intro. :sparkles:
Rhea (People Ops): PRE-START (48-72h)
- Confirm shipping address + OS + dongle preferences with IT.
- Provision SSO + company email and add to repo/team Slack channels.
- Assign buddy and block first-two-weeks pairing times on calendars.
- Share a 1-page "what to read this week" with architect diagrams and runbooks.
- Create access ticket (GitHub org, Jira group, GCP dev access) and paste example body to IT.
Rhea (People Ops): FIRST 14 DAYS (day-by-day highlights)
Day 0 (eve before): Welcome email with agenda + calendar invites.
Day 1: 10:00 team welcome (20m), 1:1 with manager (60m: role expectations + 30/60/90 draft), IT/dev env kickoff (45m with buddy), lunch w/ team.
Day 2: Deep dev-env pairing (2h) — image laptop, SSH keys, dotfiles, run tests; security & privacy primer (30m).
Day 3: Read-and-review session (pair) on serving runtime design doc (60m); small safe task assigned.
Day 4: Runbooks and incident playbook walkthrough (1h); meet product liaison (30m).
Day 5: Demo onboarding task + feedback 1:1 (30m). End-of-week short retrospective (15m).
Day 6-7: Encourage light asynchronous reading + optional office hours with buddy.
Day 8: Begin ownership of small ticket; pair on CI/deploy flow (90m).
Day 9: Observe oncall rotation handoff (shadowing) and postmortem reading (45m).
Day 10: Cross-team syncs (security/devops/observability) (60m).
Day 11: Midpoint 1:1 to update 30/60/90 and blockers (30m).
Day 12: Start work on a measurable mini-project (define metric & success criteria).
Day 13: Pairing + incremental PR review practice.
Day 14: Present progress + plan for next two weeks in 30m demo + 1:1 to align on next steps.
Rhea (People Ops): 30/60/90 (metric-driven template you can paste and edit):
- 30d: "Access & envs complete; shipped 2 small PRs (tests/fixes); completed security & infra trainings; identified one low-effort reliability improvement with baseline metric."
- 60d: "Own a small infra component; deliver a plan and prototype that improves job startup time or reduces p50 latency by N%; complete oncall shadowing and own rollouts for one minor change."
- 90d: "Ship a measurable improvement (latency/cost/reliability) with before/after metrics; present roadmap for next quarter; onboard at least one peer to your area of ownership."
Rhea (People Ops): Manager best practices (copyable bullets):
- Block 3x 1hr "focus blocks" weekly for the new hire for at least first 6 weeks.
- 15min daily async check-ins week1 (Slack thread). Keep a running onboarding notes doc.
- Set up clear "first small win" task that is scoped and visible to the team.
- Check progress at 2w, 4w, and 8w; update 30/60/90 accordingly.
Ava (Eng Manager): Can you paste the exact IT ticket template please?
Luis (IT): Sure — paste this into the IT portal and attach new hire email:
```
Title: Onboarding access for new hire <Name>
Body:
- Start date: <date>
- Needs: GitHub org: "redwood-inference" (team: "inference-runtime"), Jira project: "INF-Runtime", GCP: project "redwood-dev" (dev role), SSH key setup, VPN access.
- Equipment: laptop (mac/linux) + dongle kit, VPN token if needed.
Priority: High (onboarding)
```
Luis (IT): If you need expedited SSH key setup before laptop arrives, DM me and we'll temp-provision cloud shell keys.
Jon (HR): I'll send benefits/package links and required HR forms. Reminder: I-9 + tax forms before day 7. I'll also schedule a benefits intro call in week2 if new hire opts in.
Theo (Buddy): Happy to be buddy. I can run a "first-week dev setup" pairing Tue + Thu afternoons and host weekly office hours for the first month. I'll seed a safe onboarding issue in the backlog.
onboard-bot: Created folder and templates: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/mini-sprint-manager 12 and attached a 30/60/90 editable doc.
Ava (Eng Manager): Love the 14-day granularity. Can you also give a short email template for the manager to send on Day 0 and a Slack intro for #general?
Rhea (People Ops): Yup — copy/paste below. Day-0 email (manager -> new hire):
```
Subject: Welcome to Redwood Inference — First-week plan
Hi <Name>,
Welcome to Redwood Inference! Excited to have you on the Inference team starting <date>.
Attached is a short agenda for your first two weeks and links to the getting-started docs: Serving Runtime Overview, Runbooks, and Observability Checklist. Your buddy is Theo and your 1:1s are on Mon/Wed for the first month. Please ping me or Theo if anything is missing before start.
Best,
Ava
```
Slack intro (for #general):
"Please welcome <Name> joining as Senior Infra Engineer on the Inference team! Theyll focus on job startup time & reliability. Say hi and share your best tip for new hires! :wave:"
Jon (HR): And don't forget to enroll them in the LinkedIn Learning modules we pay for: "Secure Cloud Practices" and "Incident Management Basics" — good to complete within 30 days.
Ava (Eng Manager): Anything I should avoid or anti-patterns for week1?
Rhea (People Ops): Avoid overloading with meetings — keep afternoons free for deep work. Also don't make the first task ambiguous; give a clearly defined ticket with acceptance criteria.
Luis (IT): Finally, confirm if they need a hardware token for VPN — if yes, let us know in advance so we can ship it with the laptop.
Ava (Eng Manager): All set. I'll send the email and Slack intro tonight. Thanks everyone — this is super practical. :heart:
